summary: Implemented a default-off SGLANG_HICACHE_ASYNC_LOAD_ENQUEUE path. The scheduler retains producer-slot handoff and captures start/fence events, while a FIFO loader thread performs ordered index movement and per-layer H2D enqueue. CPU recorded flags protect device-event waits, enqueue-done flags protect slot rotation and decode restore, and loader failures record/release all layers and publish an ordered acknowledgement.

tests.command: recorded-base cache-controller regression via runpy with /job/repo/python removed from sys.path
tests.what_was_measured: Both new recorded-flag and slot-enqueue APIs are absent on the recorded base; the regression errors before the change.
19 passed, 1 skipped; recorded-flag blocking, slot backpressure, asynchronous handoff/fence capture, unchanged inline dispatch, and related staged-transfer behavior.

On one AMD Instinct MI350X, a producer-stream fill followed by loader-stream event wait and D2H copy returned 4,096/4,096 values equal to 38,470; the per-layer CPU gate released only after the GPU event was recorded.

remaining_limitations: No model weights or H100 TP8 allocation were available, so end-to-end HiCache serving throughput was not remeasured locally. The +8.8% throughput and other H100 TP8 figures remain upstream-reported results and are not local measurements. The local GPU check validates stream/event/copy ordering on ROCm MI350X, not CUDA-specific cudaMemcpyBatchAsync performance.
